questions.stem: Where are transition metals found in the periodic table?

options.text: In Group 1 on the far left
In Group 7 on the right
In Group 0 on the far right
In the central block between Groups 2 and 3

questions.explanation: Transition metals are found in the central block of the periodic table, between Groups 2 and 3. They include common metals like iron, copper, and zinc.

questions.stem: Which property is characteristic of transition metals but NOT typical of Group 1 metals?

options.text: They are metals
They are solid at room temperature
They conduct electricity
They form coloured compounds

questions.explanation: Transition metals commonly form coloured compounds (e.g., blue copper sulfate, green iron(II) compounds). Group 1 metals typically form white or colourless compounds.

questions.stem: Compared to Group 1 metals, transition metals generally have:

options.text: Lower melting points and lower densities
Lower reactivity and lower melting points
Higher melting points, higher densities, and greater hardness
The same melting points and densities

questions.explanation: Transition metals are harder, denser, and have higher melting points than Group 1 metals. They are also less reactive and stronger, making them useful as structural materials.

questions.stem: What does it mean that transition metals have 'variable oxidation states'?

options.text: Their oxidation state changes with temperature
They can only form one type of ion
They cannot form ions at all
They can form ions with different charges (e.g., Fe²⁺ and Fe³⁺)

questions.explanation: Transition metals can form ions with different charges. For example, iron can form Fe²⁺ (iron(II)) and Fe³⁺ (iron(III)) ions. This is why Roman numerals are used in their compound names.

questions.stem: Many transition metals are used as catalysts. Which transition metal is used in the Haber process?

options.text: Iron
Nickel
Copper
Zinc

questions.explanation: Iron is used as the catalyst in the Haber process for manufacturing ammonia. The ability to act as catalysts is a key property of transition metals.

questions.stem: Why are transition metals less reactive than Group 1 metals?

options.text: They do not lose electrons as easily because of their higher nuclear charge and more complex electron arrangement
They have fewer electrons
They have fewer electron shells
They are gases at room temperature

questions.explanation: Transition metals hold onto their electrons more tightly than Group 1 metals due to higher nuclear charges and more complex electronic configurations, making them less reactive.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a use of copper that depends on its properties as a transition metal?

options.text: Filling balloons, because copper is lighter than air
Electrical wiring, because copper is an excellent conductor of electricity
Water purification, because copper kills all bacteria
Making window glass, because copper is transparent

questions.explanation: Copper is widely used in electrical wiring because it is an excellent conductor of electricity and is ductile (can be drawn into wires). These are typical properties of transition metals.
